Motion perception deficits in schizophrenia are not primarily caused by eye-tracking abnormalities. While it is true that impaired eye movements can contribute to overall cognitive and perceptual problems, including motion perception issues, the condition itself appears to affect generating or integrating feedback information from eye movements.

In fact, studies have shown that patients with schizophrenia exhibit normal speed discrimination, a key component of motion perception. This suggests that the problem lies elsewhere, possibly in other aspects of motion processing or integration.

Researchers note that concurrent measurement of eye movements can provide valuable insights into interactions between these two systems and highlight the importance of considering multiple factors when studying motion perception abnormalities in schizophrenia.

While eye-tracking abnormalities may be present in some individuals with schizophrenia, it is not a primary cause of motion perception deficits. The condition's specific effects on motion perception likely result from broader cognitive and perceptual impairments unique to schizophrenia.
